evaluations.note: 30 on the reference machine (2026-10-07, 3 repeated runs identical). BFGS reaches the upper bound RCUT2B = 6.0 at eval 7 (the best, 1.015561e-01), takes the one-sided gradient there (evals 8-9), and from eval 10 its line search re-evaluates the clamped bound until MAXEVAL = 30 (status "DLIB:BFGS: MAXEVAL reached", 'MAXEVAL=30 reached'; COMPLETED until 2026-10-07); example 01, the same search with the other cohesive-energy script, ends after 12 (16 before each finite-difference gradient took the loss at its point as its centre). Whether BFGS's line search accepts a re-evaluation of the clamped bound depends on the sign of the ~1e-13 relative re-evaluation noise of the warm-started lattice relaxation, so the count is not pinned (evals_tol 18: 12..30, MAXEVAL being 30, see tolerance_rationale); best loss, components and RCUT2B do not depend on it.

tolerance_rationale: Best loss, components and RCUT2B are pinned at the default tolerances. The evaluation count is not deterministic across machines: the optimum is on the clamped bound RCUT2B = 6.0 (eval 7), and whether DLIB:BFGS's line search accepts a re-evaluation there depends on the sign of a ~1e-13 relative, rounding-level drift of the warm-started lattice relaxation. The run goes on to MAXEVAL = 30 on the reference machine (2026-10-07, 3 repeated runs identical) or stops after 12 (as example 01 does with the same search; 16 before each finite-difference gradient took the loss at its point as its centre instead of evaluating the point again), and a 1-ulp change of the hot_a0 start or of one training energy flips it. evals_tol 18 accepts 12..30 (MAXEVAL is 30): it was 14 (16..30) and was raised only to keep the shorter path, now 12 evaluations, accepted. Both endings are accepted: MAXEVAL, "DLIB:BFGS: MAXEVAL reached", and the shorter path's objective-delta test, "DLIB:BFGS: FTOL_ABS reached" (FTOL_ABS is 1e-7 by default; both ended COMPLETED until every HPO driver recorded why it ended, 2026-10-07).
